title: Real-time, cell-resolution guidance that makes incomplete cancer surgery uncommon

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a surgical guidance system that identifies residual malignant cells at the cut edges of a tumor while the operation is still underway. It would provide cellular detail across the operative margins, distinguish cancer from surrounding normal tissue, and locate remaining disease precisely enough for the surgeon to consider further excision during the same operation. The intended scope is the common operable solid cancers.

The defining advance would combine comprehensive coverage, cellular resolution, reliable tumor-to-normal discrimination and timely, actionable guidance. Finding an additional fluorescent lesion, classifying a selected tissue sample or imaging an excised specimen can contribute to this goal, but each establishes a narrower capability than detecting residual malignant cells throughout a surgical wound. The 2024 review distinguishes useful in situ fluorescence guidance from specimen imaging, which can provide better diagnostic performance under more controlled conditions.

significance.text: Residual malignant tissue at a surgical margin is an important contributor to local recurrence, although clear margins alone do not determine cure. A 2024 review reports initial positive margins in approximately 20% of head and neck cancer operations and involved margins in approximately 10% of breast-conservation operations. These are review-reported estimates for particular clinical settings, rather than universal rates. Existing surgical assessment already combines physical, radiological and pathological information, including intraoperative frozen sections and postoperative examination of the specimen.

If comprehensive detection enabled safe removal of residual disease, it could substantially reduce avoidable incomplete resections, repeat operations and local recurrences attributable to cells left at the cut edge. Partial fluorescence guidance already provides a concrete example of this potential: the supplied 2023 breast-lumpectomy trial abstract reports that second surgeries were avoided in 9 of 62 patients with positive margins. That result supports the clinical rationale without establishing the broader innovation's effectiveness across cancers.

Conditional impact assessment: making incomplete resection uncommon would change the reliability of surgery as a local cancer treatment. More precise guidance might also preserve healthy tissue and function, but that benefit requires clinical verification. Detection cannot guarantee safe removal when disease abuts critical structures or when additional excision would cause unacceptable harm. Consequently, even excellent imaging would not by itself establish an uncommon incomplete-resection rate.

Scope limit: this capability would address disease within the operative field. It would not eliminate malignant cells that have already disseminated, eradicate dormant cells elsewhere in the body or guarantee cure. No numerical reduction in overall cancer mortality can be inferred from the supplied margin-detection evidence.

missing_breakthrough.text: The target capability is comprehensive, real-time detection of residual malignant cells across operative margins with sufficient specificity and spatial precision to guide safe further excision. The supplied evidence documents useful but incomplete approaches at the sources' dates; it does not establish the availability or absence of this broader capability as of November 1, 2026.

Documented optical barriers include limited tissue penetration, background autofluorescence, selective accumulation of fluorescent probes in tumors, and reliable detection and interpretation of signals. A clinically useful signal must distinguish malignant tissue from normal tissue while remaining informative in the operative environment. Cellular detail in a selected field does not establish that the system has adequately examined the full margin, including disease beyond the accessible optical depth.

Available approaches are more varied than receptor- or enzyme-specific dyes. The supplied review describes receptor-targeted, intracellular-targeted, metabolic, microenvironment-sensitive and label-free approaches. Its supplement discusses ONM-100, or pegsitacianine, which exploits tumor-associated acidity across diverse tumor types. Such approaches may broaden applicability, but the supplied material does not demonstrate comprehensive single-cell margin detection. False-positive signal is a concern for actionable guidance; the narrower claim that inflammation specifically causes it is not established by the supplied reviewed texts.

Engineering synthesis: the remaining challenge includes turning detection into dependable surgical decisions. A system would need to connect its cellular findings to exact locations in the wound, maintain adequate coverage within an acceptable operating time, communicate uncertainty and avoid prompting harmful excision of healthy tissue. Its practical boundaries would need to identify margins that cannot be adequately assessed and disease that can be detected but cannot safely be removed.

current_state.text: The supplied 2023 prospective breast-lumpectomy trial demonstrates a meaningful partial capability. Pegulicianine-guided excisions removed residual tumor after standard lumpectomy in 27 of 357 patients, or 7.6%. Per-margin sensitivity was 49.3% and specificity was 85.2%. The trial met its prespecified thresholds for residual-tumor removal and specificity, but did not meet its prespecified sensitivity threshold. These measurements concern margins and patients in this application; they do not establish detection of every malignant cell.

The trial evidence available to the supplied review was a PubMed abstract rather than the full trial report. The abstract also states that randomization was not designed to provide a control group for evaluating device performance. The results therefore support additional residual-tumor detection and the reported performance measures, while leaving broader comparative outcome claims beyond what this supplied record establishes.

The 2024 review documents clinically used fluorescent agents, including 5-aminolevulinic acid, and a wider range of targeted and microenvironment-sensitive probes. It describes in situ fluorescence imaging as useful for surgical guidance and finding subclinical lesions, while ex vivo specimen imaging can achieve better diagnostic efficacy. Together with the breast trial, this supports the demonstrated component: selected applications can reveal disease missed by standard assessment. It does not establish comprehensive cellular certainty across operative margins and cancer types.

Several additional assertions in the earlier research remain unverified within the supplied evidence: FDA approval of pafolacianine for specified ovarian and lung indications, the glioma-specific history of 5-aminolevulinic acid, a 32.7% false-positive rate in an ovarian pafolacianine phase 3 experience, and confocal optical-biopsy accuracy often exceeding 80% in selected tissues. The cited Journal of Nuclear Medicine and ScienceDirect texts were not captured, so these statements are retained as unresolved reports rather than established findings. The Journal of Nuclear Medicine citation is identified in the research as 2026 and cannot substantiate attribution to a 2024 review. Missing evidence here does not show that the reported results are false.

The supplied review reports successful retention of the 2024 Nature article's full HTML, main PDF and a text-bearing supplement, superseding the earlier research note about failed full-page retrieval. Minor extraction artifacts remained, and figures were not visually inspected. Two additional supplementary PDFs contained essentially no extractable text and provide no inspectable support here. No freshness search was supplied, so the dated findings cannot establish the complete state of the field on November 1, 2026.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed initial clinical demonstration: prospective controlled surgical trials in at least two different operable solid tumors should show clinically meaningful reductions in incomplete resection and subsequent local recurrence attributable to residual disease at the margin, compared with standard care that includes usual visualization and pathology. Trials should prespecify effect sizes, recurrence follow-up, healthy-tissue removal and harms from false-positive excisions. These are proposed criteria for this innovation, not established regulatory or professional standards.
completion_criteria.label: Reduced incomplete resection and local recurrence across two solid tumors

completion_criteria.text: Proposed technical validation: independently verify cellular resolution, tumor-to-normal discrimination, depth limits, coverage of the operative margins and response time under actual surgical conditions, using pathological comparison where feasible. Evaluation should distinguish per-cell, per-region, per-margin and per-patient performance so that a strong result at one scale is not mistaken for comprehensive performance at another. Sensitivity around one half of involved margins in one cancer would not satisfy the proposed comprehensive capability.
completion_criteria.label: Independent verification of comprehensive cellular-resolution margin assessment during surgery

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and breadth requirements: independent teams and multiple clinical sites should reproduce the technical and clinical benefits across relevant tissue conditions, tumor subtypes and surgical workflows. Success in two cancers would establish initial breadth; broader validation would be needed to support applicability across common operable cancers. Finite testing can establish the breadth demonstrated, never literal detection of every malignant cell in every possible case.
completion_criteria.label: Independent multisite reproduction of technical and clinical benefits across cancers

completion_criteria.text: Proposed practical endpoint: demonstrate that incomplete resection becomes uncommon within clearly specified clinical populations, while preserving acceptable function, healthy tissue and operative time. Report residual failures separately, including missed disease, inadequately assessed margins and detected disease that cannot safely be excised. A reduction in positive margins alone would not establish lower recurrence or the title's intended outcome.
completion_criteria.label: Incomplete resection becomes uncommon in clearly specified clinical populations

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: ONC-01, mortality-reducing detection of lethal cancers while localized, concerns finding disease early enough for effective treatment; ONC-11 concerns the completeness of surgical removal once an operation is undertaken. ONC-10, distinguishing early neoplasms that will kill from those that will not, addresses whether treatment is warranted. More sensitive margin guidance does not establish a tumor's lethality or resolve overtreatment.

Roster-based synthesis: ONC-02 concerns sterilizing immune clearance of established metastatic carcinomas, while ONC-03 concerns eradication of dormant disseminated tumor cells responsible for late relapse. ONC-11 addresses local operative margins and could complement either systemic advance. It does not clear established metastases or dormant cells outside the operative field. The supplied roster provides these distinctions more precisely than the earlier shorthand linking ONC-02 to micrometastases alone.

Roster-based synthesis: ONC-04 seeks a shared malignant dependency that renewing normal tissues can spare, and ONC-05 seeks therapies that extinguish the whole clonal population. Both overlap with ONC-11's need to distinguish malignant from normal tissue and avoid leaving viable cancer behind, but their central goals concern therapeutic selectivity and population extinction. ONC-06 instead seeks stable reversion of carcinoma cells to non-malignant identity; surgical guidance identifies tissue for possible removal rather than changing its identity.

Roster-based synthesis: ONC-07 seeks body-wide delivery that alters essentially every malignant cell. Probe delivery may enable some forms of ONC-11, but signal generation within a surgical field does not demonstrate body-wide therapeutic delivery. ONC-12 seeks off-the-shelf cell therapy that matches autologous cures at ordinary scale; it is a distinct treatment and manufacturing challenge that could complement local surgery.

Roster-based synthesis: ONC-08 concerns interception of non-viral precancers before invasion, and ONC-09 concerns prophylactic immunity against common non-viral cancers. Both act earlier in disease development than ONC-11's operative-margin intervention. Their success might reduce the need for some cancer operations, while margin guidance would remain relevant to cancers requiring resection.

change_log.change: Preserved ONC-11's identity and title while defining the innovation as a proposed comprehensive cellular guidance capability.
change_log.reason: Partial fluorescence achievements support the concept's rationale without establishing that its intended outcome has been achieved.

change_log.change: Qualified the relationship between margins, cure, recurrence and safe excision; acknowledged intraoperative frozen-section assessment.
change_log.reason: Clear margins alone do not determine cure, current assessment includes intraoperative pathology, and detection does not guarantee safe resectability.

change_log.change: Retained the review-reported margin prevalence estimates and the trial's 27/357, 7.6%, 49.3% and 85.2% results; added the reported avoidance of second surgeries in 9/62 patients with positive margins.
change_log.reason: These supported quantitative details explain both the clinical opportunity and demonstrated partial benefit.

change_log.change: Added the trial abstract's access limitation and qualification about the purpose of randomization.
change_log.reason: The supplied evidence does not provide a full trial report or a device-performance control comparison.

change_log.change: Expanded the description of imaging approaches to include metabolic, microenvironment-sensitive and label-free methods, including the acidity-sensitive ONM-100 example.
change_log.reason: The supplied review contradicts an exhaustive restriction to receptor-, enzyme- or tumor-type-specific approaches.

change_log.change: Withheld inflammation-specific attribution of false positives and explicitly qualified the approval, ovarian false-positive and confocal accuracy assertions.
change_log.reason: Their specific supporting evidence was not available in the supplied reviewed texts; this limitation does not establish falsity.

change_log.change: Corrected the retrieval history and separated the 2024 Nature review from the uncaptured Journal of Nuclear Medicine citation identified as 2026.
change_log.reason: The validated review retained the Nature article's full text, while the later citation cannot support a 2024 attribution.

change_log.change: Strengthened proposed completion criteria with independent cellular validation, margin coverage, reproducibility, practical harms and broader clinical validation.
change_log.reason: Improvement in two cancers alone would not establish comprehensive cellular performance, broad applicability or uncommon incomplete resection.

change_log.change: Mapped all other roster entries to ONC-11 and corrected the shorthand description of ONC-02.
change_log.reason: The supplied roster defines ONC-02 as clearance of established metastatic carcinomas; each related innovation retains its distinct identity.

unresolved_issues: The complete state of the field as of November 1, 2026 remains unassessed because no freshness search was supplied.

The uncaptured Journal of Nuclear Medicine and ScienceDirect sources leave the stated FDA indications, glioma-specific agent history, ovarian 32.7% false-positive rate and confocal accuracy above 80% unverified within this record.
The denominator and analytical definition underlying the reported ovarian 32.7% false-positive rate cannot be determined from the supplied material.
Full trial methods, longer-term recurrence outcomes and broader comparative conclusions cannot be assessed from the supplied pegulicianine abstract alone.

The degree to which comprehensive detection could make incomplete resection uncommon, preserve healthy tissue or improve survival remains to be demonstrated, particularly where safe excision is anatomically constrained.
Specific numerical targets for acceptable residual failure, tissue removal, operative time and false-positive harms remain to be proposed and justified for each clinical setting.

The review's option to remove unverified ancillary claims was not followed literally: their numerical details were retained as explicitly unresolved reports to preserve the supplied research's quantitative information without endorsing it.
